newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM says she firm on wooing investment.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM says she firm on wooing investment.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Thursday that her four-month-old government was determined to pursue reforms and take necessary measures to attract overseas investment.

"We will do whatever is best for our people. We are trying to attract foreign investment, and I must tell you that investors are very eager to come to Bangladesh," she told a news conference on her return from the United States, where she attended the General Assembly of the United Nations.

"We met over 100 leading American investors and U.S.-based Bangladeshis willing to stake their money at home. I have told them opportunities (for investment) now fully exist and the government is taking steps to further open up," the prime minister said without elaborating.
"We are trying to restore the image of Bangladesh abroad... We are working hard for economic freedom for our people."
Hasina defended criticism by the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) for failing to raise the water-sharing dispute with India in her speech at the 51st General Assembly.

"We felt the situation did not warrant that. It's needless to unnecessarily internationalise a bilateral issue. We are trying to solve the dispute bilaterally. I am confident a solution will be found," she said.

Referring to BNP head Begum Khaleda Zia's remarks that Hasina's government was trying to appease India, the premier said Bangladesh had signed the nuclear comprehensive test ban treaty (CTBT), which India and Pakistan had not.
"This aptly reflects Bangladesh's independence in its own affairs, including international matters," Hasina said.

She avoided replying directly when asked if Bangladesh was going to buy electricity from India to cover its shortfall, a move that has been attracted strong criticism from the BNP and other opposition parties.
"We need energy to keep the wheels (of industry) running. Why not from India if conditions are favourable?" she said. "But a decision has yet to be made."
